liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Flutes Of The Chi** (2 reviews): Along with Blarney Stone, it gave listeners a hint of the band's later direction; Reviewer's first known live performance of the song, years before its studio release on White Pepper in 2000 [4][10]
- **Koko** (1 review): Opening with this song is unusual; it rarely appears on Ween setlists [2]
- **Freedom Of 76'** (1 review): Singled out by the reviewer as an especially strong performance [6]
- **Blarney Stone** (1 review): Along with Flutes of the Chi, it gave listeners a preview of where the band was heading [4]
- **Voodoo Lady** (1 review): The acoustic, stripped-down version is described as among the best stripped-down songs the reviewer has heard [4]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Koko, I'm Holding You, Flutes Of The Chi, Buenos Tardes Amigo, Blarney Stone, Baby Bitch [11]

## The recordings

- **Ween1994-09-01** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 73 min; rated 4.67/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: The recording's sound quality is limited, which the reviewer attributes to the show being played in a dorm hall; The recording is described as pretty good and pleasant to listen to [3][8]

## Around the show

- The band said they had recently seen Willie Nelson live, and the mellow, largely acoustic set was the result [2]
- The audience was quiet and mellow, with few shouted requests, and audibly laughed at some lyrics [2]
- Held in the lower-level common area of Demarest dorm on Rutgers' main New Brunswick campus, a long room [5]
- Reviewer recalls the band in matching suits but barefoot, set up facing the room's shorter width [5]
- Only about 60 people attended, sitting on the tile floor in front of the band [5]
- Rutgers student recalls a large dorm common room, an acoustic set, barefoot Dean and Gene, and the audience seated on the floor [7]
- Chocolate and Cheese had just come out; the reviewer is unsure how the band got booked [7]
- A calm Ween show is uncommon, which makes this one notable [9]
